newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Bullish VSNL issue dominates India GDRs.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Bullish VSNL issue dominates India GDRs.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts were dominated again on Tuesday by telecoms firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam (VSNL), following its strong launch on Monday, dealers said.
They said VSNL had risen again amid good institutional demand. The issue raised some $448 million before the exercise of a greenshoe option and was ten times oversubscribed.
Fund managers and traders said the success of the issue was well ahead of expectations, and the relatively low allocations were drawing in institutions as they sought to raise their holdings.
"The market was dominated by VSNL again as institutions came into the market. We have seen good two way trade," a dealer said.
He said investors had been surprised at the scale of demand for the issue. "They got a loss less stock than they expected."
VSNL GDRs were issued at $13.93 and rose to close at $16.50 on Monday. On Tuesday it rallied again to close at $17.65.
The rest of the market was steady but quiet and traders said it could pick up on Wednesday as the local market picked up following book-squaring on Tuesday.

A dealer said the GDR market was attracting fresh interest following the VSNL issue, which was previously twice delayed, and last month's budget. Players who had steered clear of India in recent months were looking to return.
He also said the issue could raise the prospects for other GDR issues, although none were on the immediate hroizon.
Indian GDRs rose 0.36 points or 0.47 percent to 77.75 on the HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI, with the premium over the local market at 17.60 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index was up 35.58 points at 3,765.78, after being closed for a market holiday on Monday.

Korean GDRs rose in line with local market gains, but traders said market sentiment remained edgy. While top line stocks such as Samsung would benefit from a recovery in DRAM prices, the outlook for others was less clear.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 2.93 points, or 5.26 percent stronger at 58.72, a premium of 38.40 percent over the local market.
The Korea Composite Index ended 21.64 points or 3.51 percent higher at 638.90.

Taiwan GDRs were up despited a falling local market. Traders said the concern in Taipei over the island's growing pork crisis was of less concern in the GDR market, which was dominated by firmer electronics shares.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 2.31 points, or 2.11 percent, better at 112.22, a premium of 0.01 percent.
The Taiwan Weighted Index shed 1.3 percent to 7,843.43.
